accepted.s: The General Secretary of the All India Trade Union Congress at the time of its formation was
accepted.x: Diwan Chaman Lal was the General Secretary of the AITUC at its formation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the organisational office-bearer from the president and founders.
accepted.sec: AITUC - founding year, place, first president, founders

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: INTUC — established by the Congress in 1947
RTUC — established in 1947 by the Congress
National Trades Union Federation — first May Day organisation
accepted.x: The Congress set up the Indian National Trade Union Congress in 1947. The AITUC moderates broke away in 1929, leading to RTUC and later the National Trades Union Federation.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation-year association and reject swapped institutional histories.
accepted.sec: AITUC - founding year, place, first president, founders

accepted.s: The first May Day in India was observed in 1923 at
accepted.x: The first May Day in India was observed at Madras in 1923 by the Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan under M. Singaravelu Chettiar.
accepted.tq: Test the place-year combination directly.
accepted.sec: AITUC - founding year, place, first president, founders

accepted.s: Who organised the first May Day in India under the Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan?
accepted.x: M. Singaravelu Chettiar organised the first May Day in India in Madras in 1923 under the Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan.
accepted.tq: Identify the organiser rather than the venue or year.
accepted.sec: AITUC - founding year, place, first president, founders

accepted.s: The Communist Party of India was formally founded in India at the Kanpur conference held on
accepted.x: The CPI was formally founded in India at Kanpur on 26 December 1925.

accepted.s: Who was associated with the organisation of the Communist Party of India at the Kanpur conference as its organiser?
accepted.x: Satyabhakta organised the Kanpur conference of 1925 at which the CPI was formally founded in India.

accepted.sec: Communist Party of India - founding, Kanpur conference, bans

accepted.s: Which one of the following was among those associated with the founding of the Communist Party of India at Tashkent?
accepted.x: M.N. Roy, Abani Mukherji and others were associated with the founding of the CPI at Tashkent in 1920.

accepted.s: The demand for complete independence was first advanced by the communists through open letters to the Congress sessions at
accepted.x: The communists advanced the demand for complete independence through open letters to the Ahmedabad session of 1921 and the Gaya session of 1922.

o: Jayaprakash Narayan and Acharya Narendra Dev

accepted.s: The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934 at
accepted.x: The Congress Socialist Party was founded at Patna in 1934 by Acharya Narendra Dev and Jayaprakash Narayan.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founding venue from later Andhra conferences and centres.

accepted.s: The principal economic and agrarian objectives of the Congress Socialist Party included
o: exclusive promotion of private foreign investment
a cooperative economy and radical land reform
a zamindari-based economy and protection of princely privileges
complete withdrawal from the Congress and support for imperial rule
accepted.x: The Congress Socialist Party worked inside the Congress for a cooperative economy and radical land reform.
accepted.tq: Infer the organisation’s programme from its stated economic and agrarian objectives.
accepted.sec: Congress Socialist Party - founders, Andhra unit, Rajakeeya Pathashala

accepted.s: The Andhra Socialist Party or Andhra Congress Socialist Party was organised in
accepted.x: The Andhra unit of the Congress Socialist Party was organised in 1934.

accepted.x: The first conference of the Andhra Congress Socialist Party was held at Guntur in 1935 under Tenneti Viswanatham.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the political schools of the Andhra Socialist movement?
accepted.x: Kothapatnam hosted a summer political school in 1937. Madanapalle and Mantena vari Palem hosted political schools in 1938.
accepted.tq: Match each centre with the correct year and type of activity.

accepted.s: The Kothapatnam political school of 1937 became notable because it was
o: shifted to Hyderabad after a communist ban
accepted.x: The Kothapatnam summer school was lathi-charged, and Prakasam protested against the incident.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive consequence associated with the named institution.
accepted.sec: Congress Socialist Party - founders, Andhra unit, Rajakeeya Pathashala

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
1. Kothapatnam — 1937
2. Madanapalle — 1938
3. Mantena vari Palem — 1938
4. Kankipadu — 1935
accepted.x: Kankipadu is associated with the Rajakeeya Pathashala established in 1939, not 1935. The other three place-year pairs are correct.
accepted.tq: Find the single place-year mismatch among closely related political schools.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following conspiracy cases in chronological order:
A. Peshawar Conspiracy Case
B. Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case
C. Meerut Conspiracy Case
accepted.x: The Peshawar cases belong to 1922–27, the Kanpur Bolshevik Case to 1924, and the Meerut Case to 1929.
accepted.tq: Place the cases by their years before comparing the sequence options.
accepted.sec: Conspiracy cases against communists

accepted.s: The Peshawar Conspiracy Cases of 1922–27 primarily concerned
o: foreign communists tried under the Public Safety Bill
workers involved in the Meerut trade union strike
Muhajirs trained in Soviet Central Asia
accepted.x: The Peshawar cases concerned Muhajirs who had received training in Soviet Central Asia.
accepted.tq: Match the conspiracy case with its distinctive group of accused persons.
accepted.sec: Conspiracy cases against communists

accepted.s: Which of the following persons was NOT among those associated with the Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case?
accepted.x: Philip Spratt was associated with the Meerut Conspiracy Case. M.N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmad and S.A. Dange were among those associated with the Kanpur Bolshevik Case.
accepted.tq: Use the accused-person association to separate Kanpur from Meerut.
accepted.sec: Conspiracy cases against communists

accepted.s: The Meerut Conspiracy Case of 1929 involved
o: 31 members of the Hyderabad State Comrades Association
accepted.x: The Meerut Conspiracy Case involved 31 labour and communist leaders, including Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Usmani and Philip Spratt.
accepted.tq: Test the exact number and category of accused persons.
accepted.sec: Conspiracy cases against communists

accepted.s: The long trial in the Meerut Conspiracy Case had the political consequence of making the accused
accepted.x: The prolonged Meerut trial made the labour and communist leaders widely regarded as martyrs.
accepted.tq: Identify the consequence rather than confusing it with a later organisational development.
accepted.sec: Conspiracy cases against communists

accepted.s: The Factories Act of 1881 was significant because it was the first factory law and particularly
o: introduced weekly holidays for all workers
provided legal status to trade unions
accepted.x: The Factories Act of 1881 was the first factory law and curbed child labour. It followed the 1875 Bombay factory commission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the earliest factory legislation from later labour laws.
accepted.sec: Labour laws

accepted.s: The Factories Act of 1891 provided for
o: compulsory arbitration in all industrial disputes
registration of trade unions and immunity from conspiracy suits
weekly holidays and limits on the working hours of women
accepted.x: The Factories Act of 1891 introduced a weekly holiday and limited the working hours of women.
accepted.tq: Match the statute with its specific labour provisions.
accepted.sec: Labour laws

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Trade Unions Act, 1926:
1. It provided for registration and legal status of trade unions.
2. It protected unions from civil and criminal conspiracy suits.
3. It originated from N.M. Joshi’s resolution of March 1921.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Act gave registered unions legal status and protection from specified conspiracy suits, following N.M. Joshi’s March 1921 resolution.
accepted.tq: Verify the Act’s provisions along with its legislative origin.
accepted.sec: Labour laws

accepted.s: The Trade Disputes Act of 1929 was described by Motilal Nehru as the
accepted.x: Motilal Nehru called the Trade Disputes Act of 1929 the “Slavery of India Bill”.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive political description attached to the legislation.
accepted.sec: Labour laws

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a provision of the Trade Disputes Act, 1929?
o: It abolished restrictions on disputes beyond purely industrial matters.
It banned sympathetic strikes and imposed long notice periods.
It granted automatic legal immunity to all strikes.
accepted.x: The Act banned sympathetic strikes, imposed long notice periods and made strikes beyond purely industrial disputes illegal.
accepted.tq: Identify the restrictive labour-law provision from the applied situation.
accepted.sec: Labour laws

accepted.s: The Public Safety Bill of 1929 was aimed particularly at
o: foreign communists such as Philip Spratt
trade union registrars under the 1926 Act
women workers covered by the Factories Act
accepted.x: The Public Safety Bill, passed alongside the Trade Disputes Act in 1929, was aimed at foreign communists such as Philip Spratt.
accepted.tq: Match the bill with its target group and historical context.
accepted.sec: Labour laws

accepted.s: The Whitley Commission, also known as the Royal Commission on Labour, was appointed in 1929 and reported in
accepted.x: The Whitley Commission was appointed in 1929 and submitted its report in 1931.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the appointment year from the reporting year.
accepted.sec: Labour laws
